subject: clockworkDog

I'm planning out a stylized clockwork dog made of brass and iron, with a boxy plated body, visible gears on the flank, a winding key on the back, rivets, jointed legs, and a detailed head and snout using the SDK's geometry primitives.

For the legs, I'm planning to use limb-based IK with hip and foot target points, bending the front elbows backward and giving the hind legs a three-segment digitigrade structure with a forward stifle and backward hock, placing foot targets just above the floor plane.

Then I'll chain each leg from shoulder to elbow to wrist as named joints parented to the spine, using the limb's computed points directly as the chain path, and build the main spine chain from hips through chest and neck up to the head.

Working out the body proportions now: setting the dog's length along Z, shoulder and hip joint heights, and leg segment lengths so the front legs (two segments, 0.24 each) and back legs (three segments) reach comfortably to feet near the ground without over-stretching the IK solver.

For the skeleton, I'm sketching a spine chain from a hips root joint through curved points up to the chest, with the head joint branching off the chest end, and thinking through how the chain function's parent/root naming should work so hips stays the actual root joint.

Now I'm working out the neck chain, running a curved path from the chest point upward and forward toward where the head joint will attach.

I'm then placing the head joint at the neck's endpoint with a forward-and-up direction, followed by a jaw joint positioned slightly below and forward of the head using a local offset.

For the tail, I'm building a backward-curling chain of joints parented off the hips, swept with a tapering brass tube and a tiny key-like tip. Then I'm setting up the leg roots, parenting front legs to the chest and hind legs to the hips, with target foot positions mirrored by side.

I'm computing distances and bend hints for each leg's segments -- front legs bending back at the elbow, hind legs bending knee-forward then hock-back across three segments -- and working out how the chain's joint names map onto each limb's points, with an extra name reserved for the tip joint at the foot.

Now I'm setting up the leg chains with parent bones (hips for hind, chest for front), sweeping tapered tube geometry along each chain for the limb shape, and placing box-shaped paw parts at each tip bone with brass cylinder caps rotated to act as knee and ankle joints.

For the head, I'm building box geometry for the skull, snout, and lower jaw attached to separate head/jaw bones, adding cone ears and glowing amber eye spheres positioned using directional words like "left," "up," and "forward" relative to the head bone so they mirror correctly on each side.

I'm sketching out the torso as a box aligned with the spine curve, figuring out its center and height so shoulders and legs attach cleanly inside it, then picking a color palette -- brass, iron, dark, amber, copper -- for the body materials with grained paint variants.

Now I'm planning the chest plate as an iron box, tapering the leg sweep radii for the thighs, and working out the vertical placement of the paw boxes so they rest flush on the ground at y=0.
